post.caption: One diamond got 22,000 name entries. In April 2019, a mine in Botswana found a rough diamond of 1,758 carats, about the size of a tennis ball. Reports say only the Cullinan, found in 1905, was bigger. X ray sorting spotted it, and it came out unbroken, with a black coating that its owner said hides parts of high quality white gem. People in Botswana sent in more than 22,000 names, and the one chosen, Sewelô, means rare find in Setswana. In 2020, Louis Vuitton announced plans for a jewelry collection from it, and five percent of retail sales will support community projects in Botswana.
